stories.headline: Karnataka estimates Rs 46,324 crore drought loss, seeks Rs 7,142 crore from Centre
stories.title: Karnataka estimates Rs 46,324 crore drought loss, seeks Rs 7,142 crore from Centre
stories.summary: Karnataka estimates Rs 46,324 crore drought loss, seeks Rs 7,142 crore from Centre
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar asked a Central team to approve Rs 7,142.64 crore in drought relief.
The appeal underscores mounting farm losses, water stress and pressure for quicker support.
Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Saturday urged the Centre to provide Rs 7,142.64 crore in drought relief, saying farmers and the wider public were facing severe hardship.
The revised demand comes after the state declared 177 taluks drought-hit and estimated losses at Rs 46,324.50 crore, according to a statement from the Chief Minister's Office.
The state had earlier sought Rs 3,705.30 crore from the Centre under National Disaster Response Fund norms.
Shivakumar made the appeal during a meeting with a Central Inter-Ministerial team led by Ajit Kumar Sahu, Joint Secretary in the Union Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
According to the statement, 217 of Karnataka's 240 taluks have been identified as drought-affected, while 177 have been officially declared drought-hit.
The government said the taluks were identified through a scientific assessment and in line with the Centre's disaster management guidelines.
"If farmers suffer, everything comes to a standstill.
Therefore, the central government should come to the aid of the state's farmers," Shivakumar said.
He said he and Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara had not seen such hardship among people in their four decades in public life.

He also said the government had convened a special legislative session to understand the problems faced by elected representatives and farmers, with around 150 MLAs raising issues from their constituencies.

stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh files SLP in Supreme Court challenging HC judgment on BC quota in local body elections
stories.title: Andhra Pradesh files SLP in Supreme Court challenging HC judgment on BC quota in local body elections
stories.summary: The High Court has set aside G.Os as the aggregate vertical reservation exceeds 50%, which the government argues fails to assess the 2026 exercise on its own factual foundation
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Andhra Pradesh government filed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) in the Supreme Court on Saturday, challenging the High Court order dated October 1 on reservation for the Backward Classes (BCs) in the local body elections.

It said the dispute raised an important question concerning the scope of the enabling power conferred upon the State Legislature under Articles 243-D(6) and 243-T(6) of the Constitution and the manner in which contemporaneous empirical material gathered by the State was to be evaluated while determining political reservation for the BCs in the institutions of local self-government.

The government argued that the impugned judgment proceeded on the premise that the reservation exercise undertaken in the year 2026 suffered from essentially the same infirmity as the earlier reservation exercise considered by the High Court in the Birru Prathap Reddy.
State of Andhra Pradesh.

The AP Panchayat Raj Act of 1994 was enacted pursuant to the constitutional framework introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, and Article 243-D(6) expressly enabled the State Legislatures to make provisions for reservation of seats and offices of Chairpersons in Gram Panchayats (GPs) in favour of the BCs.

Correspondingly, Article 243-T(6) facilitated such reservation in municipalities, and political reservation under Parts IX and IX-A of the Constitution had been recognised by the High Court as having a distinct constitutional foundation and purpose, and it was aimed at securing effective participation in democratic self-government, as distinguished from reservation in education and public employment, it was noted.

Further, the government stated that the AP Panchayat Raj Act originally provided for reservation for the BCs and was subsequently amended in 1995 to prescribe reservation of “not less than 34%” in respect of the relevant seats and offices in GPs and Mandal and Zilla Praja Parishads.
Significantly, the present reservation exercise was undertaken after the decision in Vikas Kishanrao Gawali.
State of Maharashtra, which required the State, before providing political reservation to OBCs in local bodies, to undertake a contemporaneous and rigorous empirical inquiry.
Accordingly, the State undertook a comprehensive Unified Family Survey (UFS) pursuant to G.O.Rt.

No.207, dated December 23, 2025, covering household and citizen-level information, including demographic profile, socio-economic status, education, employment, housing conditions, assets and allied parameters.

The State’s case before the High Court was expressly that population was not treated as the sole determinant of political reservation but it constituted an important empirical input, and it was in certain materially changed circumstances that the government issued G.O.Rt.

stories.headline: Missing Deadline Behind Punjab's Chief Justice Dispute
stories.title: Missing Deadline Behind Punjab's Chief Justice Dispute
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: The appointment of Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra as Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, notified on 5 September 2026, has drawn an unusually public objection from the State of Punjab, whose Cabinet resolved the next day that the appointment had been made without the State's consent.
The real question, however, is not whether Punjab's consent was required, for it plainly was not.
It is whether a State that has been asked for its views, and has not given them, can be said to have been consulted when the rules prescribe no time within which it must answer.
That question arises because the Memorandum of Procedure treats the two kinds of High Court appointment differently.
Where the Chief Justice of a High Court proposes a new judge, the State Government has six weeks to comment.
If it does not reply, paragraph 14 permits the Union to presume that the Governor, that is, the Chief Minister, “has nothing to add”, and to proceed.
Where the appointment is of the Chief Justice, paragraph 6 prescribes no period at all.

It is submitted that this gap, rather than the conduct of either party, lies at the heart of the dispute, and that it can be closed by a single amendment to a document the Government has been expected to revise since 2015.
The Collegium recommended Justice Mishra on 6 August 2026, and the Law Ministry sought Punjab's views between 10 and 12 August.
Haryana, which shares the High Court, responded, as did the Governors of both States; Punjab's elected government did not.
The Union notified the appointment on 5 September together with seven others, and the Chief Minister stayed away from the oath two days later.

The Additional Solicitor General has since maintained that a week or two was ample time for the State to respond, while Punjab's own Cabinet has acknowledged that no time limit is prescribed for the appointment of a Chief Justice.

stories.headline: India beat Malaysia 5-1 to defend Asian Games hockey gold, seal LA Olympics berth
stories.title: India beat Malaysia 5-1 to defend Asian Games hockey gold, seal LA Olympics berth
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India beat Malaysia 5-1 to retain the Asian Games hockey gold and secure direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Kakamigahara: India defeated Malaysia 5-1 in the men's hockey final at the Asian Games on Saturday to retain their gold medal and secure direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
The victory marked India's fifth Asian Games gold in men's hockey and their second consecutive title.
It was also the first time India had successfully defended the men's hockey gold at the Asian Games.
Captain Harmanpreet Singh led the scoring with two goals, converting penalty corners in the 11th and 57th minutes.
Jugraj Singh added another penalty-corner goal in the 23rd minute.
Vice-captain Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke in the 42nd minute, while Shilanand Lakra completed India's tally with a field goal in the 54th minute.
Malaysia's only goal came in the 14th minute through Shello Silverius, who scored from a field effort.
India dominated possession and territory early in the match, spending much of the opening quarter in the Malaysian half.
Malaysia settled for the silver medal, while Pakistan claimed bronze after defeating South Korea 5-3 earlier on Saturday.
The men's team's triumph came a day after India's women's team also won Asian Games gold.
The women defeated defending champions and reigning Olympic silver medallists China 1-0 on Friday to claim the title after a 44-year wait.

stories.headline: India GDP growth forecast stays at 7%: Virmani
stories.title: India GDP growth forecast stays at 7%: Virmani
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: “My forecast right now for the whole year is still the same.
7% plus or minus 1%,” Virmani told ANI on the sidelines of the Kautilya Economic Conclave.

Virmani said he had earlier raised his growth forecast from 6.5% to 7% but had simultaneously widened the uncertainty range, stressing that uncertainty is an inherent feature of macroeconomic conditions.
“Uncertainty is a fact of macroeconomic life,” he said, noting that economic forecasts can be affected by developments that were not anticipated when projections were made.
He said he had reassessed his forecast about a month ago in light of unresolved trade issues and other global factors, but decided to retain the 7% projection.
Virmani said he would not revise his full-year estimate solely on the basis of quarterly GDP data, despite India recording 7.8% growth in the first quarter of FY27.
“A lot of people saw this 7.8 and suddenly started raising their forecasts.
But I don't do that.
I have a forecast, I have a range of uncertainty,” he said.

His comments come as economists and analysts reassess India's growth outlook following the stronger-than-expected first-quarter expansion, while external factors including trade developments remain a source of uncertainty.

On the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) for UPI transactions, Virmani said the initial subsidy had played an important role in expanding UPI and creating what he described as a new public good, but argued that the system should gradually move towards a cost-based model.
“A good subsidy creates a new public good at minimum cost,” he said.
